We introduce a non-standard parameterization of quadratic splines and develop recursive online algorithms. Two formulations---quadratic and zero-order---offer tradeoff between smoothness and computational speed. Simulations demonstrate superior performance over high-gain observers and super-twisting differentiators under coarse sampling and high noise, benefiting systems where higher sampling rates are impractical.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin E. Avrachenkov, Leonid B. Freidovich

item.title: Multi-UAV Trajectory Optimization for Bearing-Only Localization in GPS Denied Environments
item.description: arXiv:2602.11116v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate localization of maritime targets by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) remains challenging in GPS-denied environments. UAVs equipped with gimballed electro-optical sensors are typically used to localize targets; however, reliance on these sensors increases mechanical complexity, cost, and susceptibility to single-point failures, limiting scalability and robustness in multi-UAV operations. This work presents a new trajectory optimization framework that enables cooperative target localization using UAVs with fixed, non-gimballed cameras operating in coordination with a surface vessel. This estimation-aware optimization generates dynamically feasible trajectories that explicitly account for mission constraints, platform dynamics, and out-of-frame events. Estimation-aware trajectories outperform heuristic paths by reducing localization error by more than a factor of two, motivating their use in cooperative operations. Results further demonstrate that coordinated UAVs with fixed, non-gimballed cameras achieve localization accuracy that meets or exceeds that of single gimballed systems, while substantially lowering system complexity and cost, enabling scalability, and enhancing mission resilience.
item.dc:creator: Alfonso Sciacchitano, Liraz Mudrik, Sean Kragelund, Isaac Kaminer

item.title: Computing and Optimizing the $H^2$-norm of Delay Differential Algebraic Systems
item.description: arXiv:2603.10734v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a Lanczos tau method for the approximation and optimization of the $H^2$-norm of time-delay systems described by delay differential algebraic equations of index one. The soundness of this approach is proven under the assumption of a finite strong $H^2$-norm. Furthermore, we prove convergence if the rational approximation of the exponential underlying the discretization is well-behaved and the discretization is stability preserving. Numerical results suggest that, for multiple delays, the method converges at cubic rate in the discretization degree for systems of retarded type and linearly for those of neutral type. In the single delay case, we note geometric convergence of the $H^2$-norm for systems of both retarded and neutral type when a symmetric basis is chosen. Explicit formulas are derived for the gradient of the approximation with respect to system parameters and delays. These allow us to compute the entire gradient using only about double the computational time of approximating the $H^2$-norm alone. We illustrate how these can be used to synthesize robust feedback controllers and stable approximate models. The article is concluded by a discussion of how the presented results extend and improve for approximations based on splines. We note acceleration of the convergence rate by a little over a full order for such a choice. Finally, we prove that a Lanczos tau method using a spline based on Legendre orthogonal polynomials preserves stability and guarantees convergence of the $H^2$-norm.
item.dc:creator: Evert Provoost, Wim Michiels

item.title: Global linear convergence of entropy-regularized softmax policy gradient beyond tabular MDPs
item.description: arXiv:2605.24939v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the global convergence of policy gradient for infinite-horizon entropy-regularized Markov decision processes (MDPs) with continuous state and action spaces. We consider log-linear softmax policies with linear function approximation, which extend the tabular softmax parameterization while retaining a tractable policy class. Under $Q^\pi_\tau$-realizability up to a state-dependent baseline for the regularized state-action value function, we establish a non-uniform Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) inequality for two different feature regimes. The non-uniformity arises through degeneracy of the state-averaged Fisher information matrix in the first feature regime and the uncentered feature second-moment matrix in the second. In both regimes we prove that these non-uniform constants can be bounded uniformly from below along the gradient flow. For full-affine-span features, we prove radial unboundedness of the KL regularizer and show that the state averaged smallest eigenvalue of the Fisher information matrix remains bounded below by an initialization-dependent positive constant. For simplex-valued features, we prove an analogous radial unboundedness result in the subspace orthogonal to the one vector and obtain an initialization dependent lower bound for the state averaged smallest eigenvalue of the uncentered second-moment matrix. These results imply global linear convergence of the regularized objective along the gradient flow, i.e., suboptimality decaying as $\mathcal{O}(e^{-Ct})$ for some $C>0$. Our analysis complements the global convergence theory of entropy-regularized softmax policy gradient beyond the tabular setting of Agarwal et al. (2020); Bhandari and Russo (2024); Mei et al. (2020).
item.dc:creator: Ziyue Chen, David \v{S}i\v{s}ka, Lukasz Szpruch

item.title: Parallel Policy-Gradient Methods for Parameter Optimization of Nonlinear Feedback Controllers
item.description: arXiv:2609.14114v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Structured feedback controllers provide stability guarantees, but their performance depends on manually tuned parameters. Policy-gradient methods offer a systematic way to tune these parameters, but evaluating the gradient is computationally expensive because it requires a sequential forward rollout of the state dynamics followed by a backward rollout of the costate dynamics. This letter develops a time-parallel policy-gradient framework for discrete-time nonlinear control-affine systems. We evaluate the policy gradient by formulating the forward state and backward costate rollouts as residual-minimization problems and solving them with Gauss-Newton (GN) iterations that use parallel associative scans. We show that global asymptotic stability and local exponential stability of the closed loop guarantee convergence of the parallel state solver without requiring bounds on Jacobian products throughout the state space. Near the exact trajectory, GN iterations converge quadratically in a neighborhood whose size is independent of the horizon T. When initialized at the equilibrium trajectory, a clipped variant converges at a linear rate that is also independent of T. We also quantify how horizon truncation and solver tolerance affect the accuracy of the policy gradient. Experiments on an LQR problem and a lossless Lorenz-96 system with saturated passivity-based control demonstrate improved closed-loop performance and computational benefits.
item.dc:creator: An Nguyen, Leilei Cui

item.title: Policy Iteration Is Not Polynomial for Deterministic Markov Decision Processes: The Price of Algorithmic Anarchy
item.description: arXiv:2609.40147v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish exponential iteration lower bounds in the number of states for Howard's policy iteration on deterministic discounted and average-reward Markov decision processes (MDPs), with a constant number of actions per state. This rules out polynomial-time complexity of Howard's policy iteration in both settings. We further prove that a Dantzig counterpart of Howard's policy iteration runs in strongly polynomial time on deterministic average-reward MDPs. Together with the known strongly polynomial bound for Dantzig's rule on deterministic discounted MDPs, these results establish an exponential separation between the two algorithms in both settings. This separation between Howard's decentralized and simultaneous selfish improvements and Dantzig's coordinated selection of a single action with the largest improvement across all states reveals a "price" of algorithmic anarchy.
item.dc:creator: Han Zhong, Yinyu Ye

item.title: Initialization Stability and Convergence of Projected Langevin Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.35369v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The entropic regularized optimal transport (EOT) plays a fundamental role in the computation of optimal transport. In \cite{CLP}, the authors proposed a gradient flow approach to EOT, and derived a projected Langevin diffusion that converges in distribution to the solution of EOT when initialized with a coupling between the two given marginals. In this paper, motivated by samplings of optimal couplings for EOT, we analyze the projected Langevin dynamics with arbitrary initial distribution, and prove that its long time behavior is the same as if it was initialized from a coupling.
item.dc:creator: Qi Feng, Nathan Sauldubois, Xin Zhang

item.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
item.description: arXiv:2611.27702v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations superimpose dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a hardware-native quantum-classical closed-loop primal-dual workflow, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields with zero auxiliary quadratic penalty couplings and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This workflow requires no slack qubits or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN drives the pre-polish trajectory-minimum raw QPU sample violation to $0.108 \pm 0.017$ at 4,560 qubits (83.3% exact feasibility after a deterministic 1-bit polish with best-incumbent tracking, reaching 47.3% of the continuous linear-programming relaxation bound), reduces high-constraint error by 6.1- to 20.1-fold over K-scaled first-order updates, attains 5.35-fold deeper feasible energies than linear programming with the identical 1-bit polish within a 4.10-s compute-only budget at 256 spins, and achieves 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the workflow is robust toward shot noise and freeze-out drift.
item.dc:creator: Chia-Ho Ou

item.title: Physics-Constrained Neural ODEs for Learning Traffic Dynamics and Trajectories from Road Entry/Exit Times
item.description: arXiv:2611.30577v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the problem of learning microscopic traffic dynamics and reconstructing vehicle trajectories from section entry/exit timestamps (EET) recorded by cameras and from the positions of a probe vehicle leading the platoon. The dynamics are difficult to recover as each vehicle's position is measured only at two points, and its trajectory between them is unknown. By combining Neural ODEs with a local density approximation, we learn a follow-the-leader model whose speed--density relation is a neural network. With such sparse data, an unconstrained network may learn physically unrealistic relations, such as negative speeds or non-zero speeds on a fully congested road. We therefore introduce a normalization that, applied to a monotone neural network with a learned regime change, enforces the endpoint conditions, guaranteeing an admissible speed--density relation while provably retaining the ability to approximate any admissible one. We validate the method on first- and second-order simulations, recovering the speed--density relation of the first-order model and reconstructing the trajectories of both models, with mean maximum position errors of 2.50~m and 2.51~m, respectively, on a 125~m road segment. On real-world ring-road data, the proposed model still yields an admissible relation, whereas both baselines violate the constraints; the large spread in the data, however, highlights the limitations of a first-order model with homogeneous driver behaviors.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Bogatov Wilkman, Karl Henrik Johansson, Matthieu Barreau
